gloss: to endure; to surpass; to get through

definitions.gloss: to endure; to weather; to get through
definitions.explanation: To bear hardship or difficult conditions and survive through them.

definitions.gloss: to surpass; to exceed; to outdo
definitions.explanation: To go beyond or exceed something in ability, quality, or quantity.

examples.japanese: {寒|さむ}さを{凌|しの}ぐためにコートを{着|き}た。
examples.english: I wore a coat to ward off the cold.

examples.japanese: {貯金|ちょきん}で{当面|とうめん}の{生活|せいかつ}を{凌|しの}いだ。
examples.english: I got by with my savings for the time being.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{実力|じつりょく}は{師匠|ししょう}を{凌|しの}ぐほどだ。
examples.english: His skill is enough to surpass even his master.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY:
Transitive verb ({他動詞|たどうし}). Takes を.

USAGE:
Sense 1 (endure) is common in expressions about weathering difficult situations:
・{寒|さむ}さを{凌|しの}ぐ - to ward off/endure the cold
・{暑|あつ}さを{凌|しの}ぐ - to cope with the heat
・{飢|う}えを{凌|しの}ぐ - to stave off hunger

Sense 2 (surpass) is often used with ほど:
・〜を{凌|しの}ぐほど - so much as to surpass ~

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
・{露|つゆ}を{凌|しの}ぐ - to take shelter from rain/weather
・{急場|きゅうば}を{凌|しの}ぐ - to get through an emergency
・{先輩|せんぱい}を{凌|しの}ぐ - to surpass one's senior

KANJI NOTE:
Can also be written as {淩|しの}ぐ, but {凌|しの}ぐ is standard.

REGISTER:
Neutral to slightly literary. Often found in written Japanese.
